correctness.rationale: The source bias-corrected recurrences telescope on a single impulse G at t=1 followed by zero gradients, giving v_t=(1-beta1)beta1^(t-1)G/(1-beta1^t) and u_t=(1-beta2)beta2^(t-1)G^2/(1-beta2^t). At t>=2 the current g_t=0 makes the published StableAdamW clipping RMS zero and its learning rate α. The normalized parameter update is α c1|G|/(sqrt(c2)|G|+epsilon); supremum over FINITE impulse amplitudes at each time is α c1/sqrt(c2). Its factor (beta1/sqrt(beta2))^(t-1) proves uniform boundedness exactly beta1^2<=beta2, with explicit finite boundary limit sqrt((1-beta1)/(1+beta1)); for beta1^2>beta2 choose t and then a sufficiently large finite G. The alternative v_t^2 detector yields a scalar cap α because its clip threshold D=sqrt(max(u,epsilon^2)) never exceeds sqrt(u)+epsilon. I independently checked recurrence/tail ratios for representative β values, separate from source randomized verifier.

The classical condition beta1^2<beta2 for Adam moment ratios is emphatically prior and not asserted as new. residual_risks: The β1²<=β2 ratio condition was already well known for ordinary Adam; only source-specific gate implications can claim originality.
Stress test uses exogenous gradient input rather than gradients generated by a fixed smooth optimization problem; typical source β settings remain bounded.
The unbounded family uses larger finite G with later t; fixed G with positive epsilon eventually decays.

value.rationale: A motivated robustness/safety property of an explicitly proposed optimizer design: large stale momentum can bypass a current-gradient clip after an impulse, with sharp parameter condition, while standard paper settings remain bounded. The result matters for selecting permissible decay parameters and contrasting two known detector choices; it does not claim real-world convergence failure.

scientific_limitations: Scalar one-coordinate model, no weight decay, α constant, epsilon>0; not a practical-configuration instability claim or convergence theorem.
